entries.why: The categories route appends two entries that are not categories: `promoted` (only when some agent is promoted) and `all`. The client recognises them by value and turns them into the list route's own filters instead of sending them as `category`.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames a sentinel or adds another, and the app sends it as a category. The list route filters on a category no agent has and answers with an empty page, so the chip shows no agents and nothing errors.

entries.why: How the web grid turns the selected chip and search into list params: `promoted` -> `promoted=1`, `all` -> no filter, anything else -> `category`; while searching, `promoted` and `all` send neither so the search covers every agent.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes which filters a search keeps (or adds a chip), and the app keeps narrowing or widening results differently from the web. Every request succeeds; the lists just disagree.

entries.why: The query parameters `GET /api/agents` reads: `limit`, `cursor` (the previous page's `after`), `search`, `category`, `promoted` (matched as the strings '1' and '0'), `requiredPermission`. A parameter it does not read is dropped without an error.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames a parameter or changes the `promoted` values, and the app's filter or paging is silently ignored: load-more re-reads the first page or Top picks shows every agent. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: The link the agent page's Copy link puts on the clipboard: the web's own agent URL, `<origin>/c/new?agent_id=<id>` (the AGENT entry's getResourceUrl). It is pasted into the web, so it must name a route the web client opens.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream moves the new-chat route or renames the agent query parameter, and a copied link opens the web on a 404 or on a new chat without the agent. Nothing in the app fails.

kotlin.symbol: AGENT_DESCRIPTION_TAGS / isAgentDescriptionHtml; HtmlDescription.kt safeHref and HtmlRenderer.tag

entries.why: Which tags an agent description may use as HTML (a, strong, b, em, i, br, code, span, p, div, ul, ol, li) and which links survive (CONFIG_HTML_SAFE_URI: http(s), mailto, tel, or relative). Detection (a description is HTML only when it starts with an allowlisted tag, decisions C7) is the separate agent-description-html-detection entry; the card strips it with core/common HtmlText.kt htmlToPlainText.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream widens or narrows the allowlist or the safe-URI rule, and the same description renders differently on the web and in the app: a tag the web styles shows as bare text, or a link the web drops becomes tappable here. Nothing errors.

entries.why: How the web decides a description is HTML at all. The rule lives in Description.tsx: `isHtmlDescription` matches `^<\s*\/?\s*([a-z][a-z0-9]*)\b` on the trimmed text and checks the tag against `descriptionHtmlTags` (CONFIG_HTML_RICH_TEXT_TAGS plus CONFIG_HTML_MEDIA_TAGS, so `img` counts). This client ports it as `isAgentDescriptionHtml` (decisions C7): only a description that starts with such a tag is HTML, so `List<String>` or a tag mid-sentence stays plain. Other upstream revisions use `description.trim().startsWith('<')` instead. The whole file is watched so a change to the regex or the tag set is seen.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes its detection, and a description the web shows as text renders as HTML here (placeholders vanish) or the reverse (markup shows raw). Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: The permission keys every role gate looks up in the served role map (USE, CREATE, UPDATE, READ, SHARE, OPT_OUT, SHARE_PUBLIC). The map arrives from the server, the key names do not. READ and OPT_OUT gate the Memories list and its opt-out switch.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames a key or moves a route onto a new one, and the lookup misses it. hasAccess is permissive on a missing key, so the app keeps offering the affordance and every use is refused with 403. No decode fails.

entries.why: The key the storage layer refuses to write: createMemory, setMemory and setMemoryById each return { ok: false } for a key equal to 'nothing' ignoring case, which the routes turn into a bare 500 ('Failed to create memory.'). 'nothing' passes MEMORY_KEY_PATTERN, so only this check stops it before the request. Watched file-level because the comparison is inline in three function bodies with no exported symbol of its own.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed or added reserved key is let through the local check and the save fails with the generic 'Couldn't save the memory' instead of a field error. A removed one keeps refusing a key the server would now take. Nothing decodes wrong.

entries.why: The 1000-character key cap the create route and the key-addressed PATCH enforce with a 400. The by-id PATCH repeats it (memory-key-max-length-by-id), and the agent tools carry their own MEMORY_KEY_CHAR_LIMIT in packages/api/src/agents/memory.ts. The client checks it locally so the field says why rather than relaying the server's English sentence. Watched file-level: the literal sits inline in two route handlers. api/server/routes/memories.js is watched file-level by memory-key-max-length, memory-char-limit-default and memory-key-route-not-found, so a DRIFT report here may be any of their literals: check all of them before dismissing it, namely the three `memoryConfig?.charLimit || 10000` fallbacks (GET /, POST /, PATCH /:key), the two `key.length > 1000` / `newKey.length > 1000` caps (POST /, PATCH /:key) and the two `'Memory not found.'` 404s (PATCH /:key, DELETE /:key). The generateCheckAccess pairs at the top of the file have block entries of their own (memory-route-check-*).
entries.failure_mode: A raised cap leaves the client refusing keys the server would take; a lowered one lets a key through to a 400 whose English text is shown verbatim. No decode fails.

entries.why: The per-value character cap the memory routes fall back to when the deployment configures none: `memoryConfig?.charLimit || 10000` in GET / (the envelope's charLimit), POST / and PATCH /:key. The memory sheet counts the value against it and blocks Save over it whenever the envelope leaves charLimit out (v0.8.8 always sends it). The by-id PATCH repeats the literal (memory-char-limit-default-by-id). Watched file-level: the literal is inline in three handlers. api/server/routes/memories.js is watched file-level by memory-key-max-length, memory-char-limit-default and memory-key-route-not-found, so a DRIFT report here may be any of their literals: check all of them before dismissing it, namely the three `memoryConfig?.charLimit || 10000` fallbacks (GET /, POST /, PATCH /:key), the two `key.length > 1000` / `newKey.length > 1000` caps (POST /, PATCH /:key) and the two `'Memory not found.'` 404s (PATCH /:key, DELETE /:key). The generateCheckAccess pairs at the top of the file have block entries of their own (memory-route-check-*).
entries.failure_mode: A changed default makes the sheet block values the server would take, or let an over-limit value through to a 400 whose English text is shown verbatim. Only a server that omits charLimit is affected. No decode fails.

entries.why: The by-id PATCH's copy of the same fallback, `req.config?.memory?.charLimit || 10000` (see memory-char-limit-default). The sheet edits through this route whenever the memory has an id. Watched file-level: the literal is inline in the handler. packages/api/src/memory/handlers.ts is watched file-level by memory-char-limit-default-by-id, memory-key-max-length-by-id and memory-by-id-not-found, so a DRIFT report here may be any of their literals: check all of them before dismissing it, namely the PATCH handler's `req.config?.memory?.charLimit || 10000` and `key.length > 1000`, and the two `'Memory not found.'` 404s (PATCH /id/:id, DELETE /id/:id).
entries.failure_mode: The by-id route moves its default apart from the key routes, and an edit is checked against the wrong cap. No decode fails.

entries.why: The agent-partition middleware answers a write to an agent's memories with 404 'Agent not found.' or 403 'Agent access denied.' under `error`, with no code. The text is the only thing separating that 404 from 'Memory not found.' or a missing by-id route, and that 403 from a role refusal. MemoryRepositoryImpl uses the 404 to skip the key-route fallback (the key route sits behind the same middleware), and the Memories page matches both to show its own 'This agent's memories can't be changed'.
entries.failure_mode: Reworded text makes the by-id 404 fall back to the key route (one wasted request, same refusal) and falls through to the generic save/delete failure (404, with a needless reload) or the role-permission string (403): the user is told the wrong reason. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The by-id PATCH and DELETE handlers answer a row that is gone with 404 'Memory not found.' under `error`, with no code. MemoryRepositoryImpl reads that text to tell the handler's 404 from a missing route (a pre-rc2 server's Express default 404 has no JSON `error`) and returns it instead of falling back to the key route; MemoryFailureMapping.isNotFound reads it to treat a delete of a row already gone as done and to turn an edit of one into a re-add. The key routes send the same text (memory-key-route-not-found). Watched file-level: the literal is inline in both handlers. packages/api/src/memory/handlers.ts is watched file-level by memory-char-limit-default-by-id, memory-key-max-length-by-id and memory-by-id-not-found, so a DRIFT report here may be any of their literals: check all of them before dismissing it, namely the PATCH handler's `req.config?.memory?.charLimit || 10000` and `key.length > 1000`, and the two `'Memory not found.'` 404s (PATCH /id/:id, DELETE /id/:id).
entries.failure_mode: Reworded text makes a by-id 404 for a deleted row fall back to the key route, which edits, or for a rename replaces, any row re-created elsewhere with the same key. The user's other memory is silently overwritten; nothing errors.

entries.why: The key-addressed PATCH /:key and DELETE /:key answer a row that is gone with 404 'Memory not found.' under `error`, the same text as the by-id handlers (memory-by-id-not-found). The Memories page goes through these routes on a server without the by-id routes (pre-rc2) and for a memory with no id. MemoryFailureMapping.isNotFound matches the text: a delete that answers it counts as done (the row goes, no error), and an edit that answers it removes the row and offers the draft as a re-add. Watched file-level: the literal is inline in both handlers. api/server/routes/memories.js is watched file-level by memory-key-max-length, memory-char-limit-default and memory-key-route-not-found, so a DRIFT report here may be any of their literals: check all of them before dismissing it, namely the three `memoryConfig?.charLimit || 10000` fallbacks (GET /, POST /, PATCH /:key), the two `key.length > 1000` / `newKey.length > 1000` caps (POST /, PATCH /:key) and the two `'Memory not found.'` 404s (PATCH /:key, DELETE /:key). The generateCheckAccess pairs at the top of the file have block entries of their own (memory-route-check-*).
entries.failure_mode: Reworded text on the key routes makes deleting a memory already gone show a generic failure whose Retry can only fail again, and an edit of a deleted memory a generic error instead of the re-add. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The by-id PATCH's copy of the 1000-character key cap, `key != null && key.length > 1000`, answered with a 400 (see memory-key-max-length for the key routes). A rename through the sheet goes through this handler whenever the memory has an id, and the sheet checks MEMORY_KEY_MAX_LENGTH locally so the field says why. Watched file-level: the literal is inline in the handler. packages/api/src/memory/handlers.ts is watched file-level by memory-char-limit-default-by-id, memory-key-max-length-by-id and memory-by-id-not-found, so a DRIFT report here may be any of their literals: check all of them before dismissing it, namely the PATCH handler's `req.config?.memory?.charLimit || 10000` and `key.length > 1000`, and the two `'Memory not found.'` 404s (PATCH /id/:id, DELETE /id/:id).
entries.failure_mode: The by-id cap moves apart from the key routes' and a rename is checked against the wrong length: refused locally when the server would take it, or let through to a 400 whose English text is shown verbatim. No decode fails.

entries.why: The permission pair the memory routes' checkMemoryRead middleware requires for GET / (the list and its usage envelope): USE + READ. The role map is served, the pair each route checks is not. The client offers the action only when the role holds the same pair (permissive on a missing key): canOpenMemories() in core/model UserRolePermissions.kt: the Data tab's Memories row and its count fetch (DataSettingsViewModel), the Memories page itself (MemoriesUiState.canRead) and the chat memory card's Manage action (ChatConfigDelegate memoriesPageEnabled).
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the pair (adds a DELETE bit, moves a route onto another check) and the UI keeps offering an action the server refuses with 403, or hides one the server would allow. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The permission pair the memory routes' checkMemoryCreate middleware requires for POST / (create): USE + CREATE. The role map is served, the pair each route checks is not. The client offers the action only when the role holds the same pair (permissive on a missing key): canMemories(Permission.CREATE) in MemoriesViewModel.derive (MemoriesUiState.canCreate): the Add button, the FAB and the empty state's action.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the pair (adds a DELETE bit, moves a route onto another check) and the UI keeps offering an action the server refuses with 403, or hides one the server would allow. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The permission pair the memory routes' checkMemoryUpdate middleware requires for PATCH /:key and PATCH /id/:id (edit and rename): USE + UPDATE. The role map is served, the pair each route checks is not. The client offers the action only when the role holds the same pair (permissive on a missing key): canMemories(Permission.UPDATE) in MemoriesViewModel.derive (MemoriesUiState.canUpdate): the card's menu and an editable sheet; without it the sheet opens read-only.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the pair (adds a DELETE bit, moves a route onto another check) and the UI keeps offering an action the server refuses with 403, or hides one the server would allow. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The permission pair the memory routes' checkMemoryDelete middleware requires for DELETE /:key and DELETE /id/:id: USE + UPDATE (there is no DELETE bit). The role map is served, the pair each route checks is not. The client offers the action only when the role holds the same pair (permissive on a missing key): canMemories(Permission.UPDATE) in MemoriesViewModel.derive (MemoriesUiState.canUpdate): Delete sits in the same menu as Edit.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the pair (adds a DELETE bit, moves a route onto another check) and the UI keeps offering an action the server refuses with 403, or hides one the server would allow. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The permission pair the memory routes' checkMemoryOptOut middleware requires for PATCH /preferences (the opt-out switch): USE + OPT_OUT. The role map is served, the pair each route checks is not. The client offers the action only when the role holds the same pair (permissive on a missing key): canMemories(Permission.OPT_OUT) in MemoriesViewModel.derive (MemoriesUiState.canOptOut): the "Use saved memories" switch card.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the pair (adds a DELETE bit, moves a route onto another check) and the UI keeps offering an action the server refuses with 403, or hides one the server would allow. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Whether a run gets the inline memory tools: the agents endpoint's memory capability, memory enabled in the deployment config, the user not opted out (personalization.memories !== false), and the role holding MEMORIES USE + CREATE + UPDATE. The composer's memory toggle and the request's ephemeralAgent.memory follow the same gate (ChatConfigDelegate memoryEnabled, ChatUiState.isMemoryToolAvailable, ChatRequestBuilder), so a role the server would refuse never sees the toggle.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the permission set or adds a condition and the toggle shows for a role whose send the server silently runs without memory (the user believes the chat is remembering), or hides for one the server would allow. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The `error` value of a 400 the content filter returns for a memory write (contentFilterBlockResponse: { error: 'content_filter_block', message, source, field }). The page shows its own localized string on this code instead of the English `message`. Watched file-level: the literal is inside the function body.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed code makes a filtered write show the server's English sentence verbatim (as any other 400) instead of the localized string. Nothing errors.

entries.why: How full the personal memory pool reads on the Memories page: over 90% the error colour, over 75% the warning colour, else success, applied to the server's usagePercentage. The server sends the number, not the grade.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream moves a threshold and the pill and bar grade the same usage differently from web (amber where web is red). Nothing errors.

entries.why: The five MEMORIES permission keys the admin Memory permissions screen writes with PUT /api/roles/:roleName/memories (USE, CREATE, UPDATE, READ, OPT_OUT). The route parses the body with memoryPermissionsSchema.partial() and merges it onto the stored role; the key set is never served.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames or adds a key and zod strips what it does not know: the save returns 200 with the role unchanged (or the new permission is never offered), so the admin's switch silently does nothing. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The four SKILLS permission keys the admin Skills permissions screen writes with PUT /api/roles/:roleName/skills (USE, CREATE, SHARE, SHARE_PUBLIC); RoleSkillsAdminViewModel.save() maps its switches onto them. The route (createPermissionUpdateHandler('skills') in api/server/routes/roles.js) parses the body with skillPermissionsSchema.partial() and merges it onto the stored role; the key set is never served.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames or adds a key and zod strips what it does not know: the save returns 200 with the role unchanged (or the new permission is never offered), so the admin's switch silently does nothing. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The share dialog's 'Share files' switch starts ON for a conversation with no link (and for a legacy link that stored no choice), and an existing link shows its stored snapshotFiles. The default sits in a useState and a useEffect inside the component, which the block extractor cannot isolate, so the whole file is watched; churn elsewhere in the dialog (QR, layout, target resolution) reports DRIFT -- check the snapshotFiles state, not the file. The controller seeds a new link from FilesOption.NEW_LINK and an existing one from the lookup's snapshotFiles ?: true, and sends the value on Create and on every Update (see share-update-snapshot-files-reset).
entries.failure_mode: Web flips the default to off and the app keeps publishing every new link with the chat's images and files, or the reverse. Nothing errors.

entries.why: A shared link's public URL is `<apiBaseUrl>/share/<shareId>`, built client-side; the server only returns the shareId. The app builds it from the active server's cleaned base URL in one place.
entries.failure_mode: Web moves the viewer route (or adds a prefix) and every link the app copies, shows as a QR code or hands to the system share sheet opens a 404. Nothing errors in the app.

entries.why: A tapped or shared-in link opens the in-app viewer only when it reads as `<server>/share/<shareId>`: the web client's `share/:shareId` route under the deployment's base path, one id segment. Anything else goes to the browser (taps) or the composer (share-to).
entries.failure_mode: Web moves or renames the viewer route and links to it stop opening in the app (they go to the browser instead), or the app opens a path web no longer treats as a share. Nothing errors.

entries.why: GET /api/share accepts sortBy createdAt|title and sortDirection asc|desc, inline in the list handler, and silently falls back to createdAt desc on anything else; a cursor is only valid for the sort that made it (400 otherwise). The handler is an anonymous route callback the block extractor cannot isolate, so the whole route file is watched; the same file carries the error-code table and the PATCH snapshotFiles rule, so DRIFT here may belong to either of those entries -- check the GET '/' handler.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed sort key makes the app's Oldest / Title order silently come back newest-first, or a cursor rule change makes load-more 400.

entries.why: The shared-links list 400s a trimmed search longer than this. The repository trims and cuts the query to it before sending.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream lowers the cap and long searches fail with a 400 the list shows as a load error; raises it and the app cuts searches the server would have taken.

entries.why: The share routes answer {message, code} and the code decides what the sheet says and does: TARGET_MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND / NO_MESSAGES trigger the one re-resolved retry and their own messages, SHARE_EXISTS is answered with a lookup, SHARE_REVISION_MISMATCH is the viewer's 'link was updated', *_NOT_FOUND read as removed. The codes are strings on the wire with no schema.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed or new code falls through to the generic error: the saved-target retry stops firing, or a 409 that should be adopted shows 'Something went wrong'.

entries.why: PATCH /api/share/:shareId re-derives snapshotFiles from the request on every update (`isFileSnapshotEnabled(config) && requested !== false`), so an update without snapshotFiles turns files back ON for a link that had them off. The controller therefore always sends the link's stored choice (from the lookup) or the user's new one. Lives inside an anonymous route handler, so the whole file is watched -- check the PATCH handler's snapshotFiles line.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream starts preserving the stored value on omission nothing breaks; if it changes the default or the field name, updates silently publish files the user turned off, or drop files they wanted.

entries.why: A content-filter refusal on the share routes is a 400 with {error: 'content_filter_block', message, source, field} and no code. The sheet keys 'Your server blocked sharing this content' plus the server's sentence on that error id.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed error id makes a filter refusal read as a generic failure, hiding the server's explanation of what to remove.

entries.why: The other content-filter body the share routes send (also ContentTraversalLimitError in protection/adapters/nested.ts uses the same id): {error: 'content_filter_uninspectable', ...}, 400, no code.
entries.failure_mode: Same as share-content-filter-block, for files the filter couldn't inspect.

entries.why: Fork from a share: targetMessageIndex is the index of the active branch tip in the snapshot's messages and the server copies the direct path to it; shareRevision is the snapshot's updatedAt, a mismatch is 409 SHARE_REVISION_MISMATCH, and WITHOUT a revision the index is ignored and the whole share is copied. So the viewer must send both.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the index basis (e.g. to ids) or the revision rule, and Continue silently forks the wrong branch or the whole share.

entries.why: Continue from a shared link forks the branch on screen: web walks the shared tree from the root, taking the chosen sibling at each level and the newest by default, and sends the index of the tip it reaches in the snapshot's messages (ShareView.tsx getActiveTargetIndex). The viewer takes the last node of buildActiveMessagePath, whose default is also the newest sibling, and looks up its index the same way.
entries.failure_mode: Web changes which sibling a branch defaults to, or what the tip is, and Continue in the app copies a different branch from the one web would for the same screen. Nothing errors.

entries.why: From the open chat, web sends the active branch's latest message as targetMessageId (ShareButton.tsx resolveTargetMessageId, after confirming it is saved) and, on TARGET_MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND or NO_MESSAGES, re-resolves and retries exactly once (publishWithTailRetry here). Sharing any other conversation sends no target. The retry lives in a module-level arrow function the extractor can isolate, but the error-code helper beside it matters too, so the file is watched.
entries.failure_mode: Web changes which message it targets or drops the retry, and the app shares a different cut of the chat than web would, or keeps retrying where web gives up. Nothing errors.

entries.why: A file whose source is 'text' has no stored bytes; the shared-link file route serves its extracted text as text/plain. The viewer opens such files as text.
entries.failure_mode: The value is renamed and text-only files in a shared chat try to open as binary downloads that fail.

entries.why: A shared link's ACL has two roles: sharedLink_viewer, which every grant and public access take, and sharedLink_owner, which is shown locked and never offered (web filters it from AccessRolesPicker and locks the row in SelectedPrincipalsList). The access section also labels a role by its id's _viewer / _editor / _owner suffix, since the roles route returns i18n keys (com_ui_role_viewer) as names.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames a role id or adds a shared-link role, and the editor offers the owner role, grants a role that no longer exists (the PUT fails), or labels roles by their raw ids.

entries.why: Any PUT that grants sharedLink_owner, or adds or removes the link's owner as a user, is refused with 400 {error:'Bad Request', message:'Shared link owner permissions cannot be changed'}. The body carries no code, so the client matches that exact message to say 'The owner's access can't be changed' instead of a generic failure.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream rewords the message or adds a code, and an owner-protection refusal reads as 'Couldn't update access. Try again.', inviting a retry that can never succeed.

entries.why: In the PUT body, public:true with publicAccessRoleId grants public access, public:false (strictly false) revokes it, and an absent public leaves it alone. The share-policy middleware checks SHARE_PUBLIC whenever public is true, so the editor sends public only when public access is what changes (web's sendPublicUpdate rule), never echoed on a grant or revoke. UpdateResourcePermissionsRequest.public is nullable so false survives encodeDefaults=false.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream starts reading an absent public as false (every grant would turn public access off) or changes the revoke test, and public access flips without the user touching the switch.

entries.why: POST /api/share/:conversationId reads grantPublic = role.permissions.SHARED_LINKS.SHARE_PUBLIC === true and passes it to grantCreationPermissions, which adds the PUBLIC viewer grant only when it is true. Without that grant only the owner and explicit ACL principals can open the link; with it, anyone (ALLOW_SHARED_LINKS_PUBLIC, publicSharedLinksEnabled) or any signed-in user. The sheet's who-can-open note for a new link follows that rule, fail-closed on an unknown role.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes who gets the creation-time public grant (another permission bit, a default, a config switch), and the sheet promises access the server never grants, or hides access it does. Nothing errors; a colleague just gets a 403.

entries.why: grantCreationPermissions grants OWNER to the creator and SHARED_LINK_VIEWER to PUBLIC only when grantPublic is true; see share-public-grant-rule for where grantPublic comes from.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream grants the public viewer role unconditionally or to another principal, and the sheet's 'Only you and the people you add' note becomes wrong.

entries.why: Changing a resource's ACL needs the role's <type> SHARE (checkShareAccess, sharedLink -> SHARED_LINKS) and, for public:true, SHARE_PUBLIC (checkSharePublicAccess), each strictly === true. The client gates the Manage access row on SHARED_LINKS.SHARE and the public switch on SHARED_LINKS.SHARE_PUBLIC, fail-closed to match.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream maps sharedLink to another permission type or relaxes a check, and the app hides controls the server would allow or shows ones it refuses with a 403.

entries.why: search-principals is behind checkPeoplePickerAccess: a non-admin may search only the principal types whose PEOPLE_PICKER permission (VIEW_USERS, VIEW_GROUPS, VIEW_ROLES) is strictly true, and gets a 403 when none is. The editor shows people search with any of the three and sends no type filter, so the server searches whatever the role allows.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames the permissions or changes the mapping, and the search box disappears for people who may search, or shows and only ever fails.

entries.why: search-principals answers 400 'Query must be at least 2 characters long' when the trimmed q is shorter than 2 (web's people search is enabled only from 2 characters). AclController sends no search below that length, and the editor shows neither an error nor 'no matches' for it.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream raises the minimum, and every query below the new length shows 'Couldn't search' instead of waiting for more letters.

entries.why: Web offers Manage access on a shared link only when the role has SHARED_LINKS.SHARE (useHasAccess, false on unknown), the link's effective permissions (GET /api/permissions/sharedLink/:_id/effective) include the SHARE bit, and the lookup returned the link's _id. The sheet's row follows the same three conditions.
entries.failure_mode: Web changes the gate, and the app offers a page whose reads the server refuses, or hides it from people web lets in.

entries.why: Whether a skill is active for the user: override, then deployment, then no-user fails closed, then owner, then defaultActiveOnShare. The detail switch and the list's Off badge show it, and the toggle writes against it.
entries.failure_mode: The switch shows a skill on (or off) while the server's runs treat it the other way, and the toggle stores or deletes the wrong override. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Web's default (deployment or owned on, shared follows defaultActiveOnShare, `source === 'deployment'` on the wire) and its rule that a toggle landing on the default deletes the key instead of storing it. Both live in this hook, so the whole file is watched.
entries.failure_mode: Redundant overrides pile up until the server's 200-entry cap refuses every toggle, or a deployment skill reads as shared because the wire marker moved.

entries.why: How `interface.skills.defaultActiveOnShare` is read: object form only, explicit true only.
entries.failure_mode: Shared skills show the wrong default for every user on a server that sets it.

entries.why: Owner (author === user.id) or ADMIN counts as every ACL bit; otherwise the per-skill bits decide. `export default function` is not a block anchor, so the whole file is watched.
entries.failure_mode: Edit/Delete/Share offered to users the server refuses (403 on tap), or hidden from users it allows.

entries.why: Which middleware guards each route: PATCH and DELETE run checkSkillCreate (role CREATE) before the ACL check; the file routes run the ACL EDIT check alone. The client's canEdit/canDelete carry CREATE and canEditFiles does not because of this order.
entries.failure_mode: A gate the route gained or dropped: buttons that 403, or edits hidden from users who may make them.

entries.why: Every non-VIEW route on a deployment skill answers 403 'Deployment skills are read-only', ahead of the ACL and of admin, so the client offers nothing on one.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream lets admins edit deployment skills, the client keeps hiding the actions; if it locks more, the client offers actions that 403.

entries.why: `PUT /api/permissions/skill/:id` runs checkShareAccess, which needs role SKILLS.SHARE on top of the ACL SHARE bit (ResourceType.SKILL maps to PermissionTypes.SKILLS here).
entries.failure_mode: The sharing sheet is offered to a user whose role can't share (every change 403s), or hidden from one who can.

entries.why: `PUT /api/permissions/agent/:id` runs checkShareAccess, which needs role AGENTS.SHARE (ResourceType.AGENT maps to PermissionTypes.AGENTS here) before the owner's ACL SHARE bit is even read, and checkSharePublicAccess, which needs AGENTS.SHARE_PUBLIC only for `public: true`. The agent editor's sharing section is drawn only with SHARE (or ADMIN, which skips checkShareAccess via checkShareAccessUnlessAgentAdmin) and its public switch only with SHARE_PUBLIC.
entries.failure_mode: The agent sharing section offers a public switch, grants and revokes that 403 for a stock USER role, or hides them from a role upstream newly lets share.

entries.why: Web offers an agent's share dialog only when `(agent.author === user.id || isAdmin || hasPermission(SHARE)) && (hasAccessToShareAgents || isAdmin)`, the SHARE bit read from the viewer's effective permissions on the agent's `_id`. The agent editor's sharing section copies that condition, because GET and PUT /api/permissions/agent/:id both run checkResourcePermissionAccess(SHARE). Watched as a whole file because the component is a default export the block extractor can't anchor on.
entries.failure_mode: An editor without the SHARE bit is shown a sharing section whose grants fetch and every change 403, or a viewer upstream newly lets share sees no section. Nothing errors in the client.

entries.why: For ResourceType.AGENT the permissions routes call canAccessResource with no idResolver, so `:resourceId` must be the agent's database `_id` (web passes `resourceDbId={agent._id}`); an `agent_…` id never matches an ACL entry and checkPermission answers false. The effective/all map the share gate reads is keyed the same way. The skill branch has an idResolver, which is why the skills sheet can pass its id as it is.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream adds an agent idResolver nothing breaks; if it starts keying by `agent_…` id, the sharing section 403s or 404s for everyone but admins and the share gate finds no bits.

entries.why: `GET /api/permissions/search-principals` with no type passes for the ADMIN role, otherwise needs PEOPLE_PICKER VIEW_USERS, VIEW_GROUPS or VIEW_ROLES (all false for USER by default). The skill share sheet and the agent sharing section (both via canSearchPeople) offer the people search only then, as web's usePeoplePickerPermissions does.
entries.failure_mode: A sharing UI shows a search that 403s on every query ("Search failed" with a Retry that can't succeed), or hides it from a role upstream newly lets search.

entries.why: The path a file upload may use: at most 500 chars of ASCII [a-zA-Z0-9._-/], no empty/./.. segment, no leading slash, not SKILL.md. The client sanitizes a picked filename to it.
entries.failure_mode: A filename the client lets through comes back as a bare 400 'Invalid file path'.

entries.why: The upload handler refuses `relativePath.toUpperCase() === 'SKILL.MD'` (any letter case, stricter than validateRelativePath) and has no rename for it, so the client refuses it before uploading.
entries.failure_mode: A picked skill.md uploads to a 400 the user can't act on, or the client refuses a name the server would now accept.

entries.why: `GET /api/categories` labels each built-in category with a web localization key (`com_ui_idea`), not text, so the app translates the built-in values itself. A label that isn't a `com_` key is shown as sent.
entries.failure_mode: A category upstream adds or renames shows its raw stored value (`teach_or_explain`) on the skill cards instead of a translated label. Nothing errors.

entries.why: `GET /api/permissions/{skill,agent}/roles` names each role with a web localization key (`com_ui_role_viewer`), not text, so the skill sharing sheet and the agent editor's sharing section translate the seeded roles by key, and by `skill_*` / `agent_*` id for a grant whose role isn't in the list. A name that isn't a `com_` key is shown as sent. MCP servers and remote agents seed keys of their own and aren't covered.
entries.failure_mode: A skill or agent role upstream adds or renames shows its raw id or key (`skill_editor`, `com_ui_role_viewer`) in the sharing role menus. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Web starts a new grant and public access at the resource config's `defaultViewerRoleId` (`skill_viewer`, `agent_viewer`). The skill sheet and the agent sharing section do the same, falling back to the role with the fewest permission bits: the roles route doesn't sort, so the list's first role may be owner.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed viewer id makes new grants start at whichever role has the fewest bits, or web and the app default people to different roles.

entries.why: A create onto a taken name answers 409 with the sentence 'A skill with this name already exists' as `error`; the client matches it exactly to show the Name field error.
entries.failure_mode: A reworded sentence turns name collisions into a generic error banner.

entries.why: PATCH has two 409 bodies, told apart by `error`: 'skill_version_conflict' with `current`, and the name-taken sentence. The repository branches on it.
entries.failure_mode: A new 409 body, or a renamed code, reads as a generic error; a version conflict without `current` can't be rebased.

entries.why: The states POST refuses a map that, after pruning, holds more than 200 overrides with 400 `code: 'MAX_SKILL_STATES_EXCEEDED'`. The repository matches the code to show its own 'set some back to their default' message instead of the server's English sentence.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed code shows the server's untranslated sentence as a generic toggle failure, with no hint of what to do. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The raw-payload check refuses more than 400 entries with 400 `code: 'SKILL_STATES_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE'`; the client reads it as the same too-many-overrides refusal.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed code shows the server's untranslated sentence as a generic toggle failure. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Brand namespaces a skill name may not start with. The editor flags them on the Name field before Save.
entries.failure_mode: A prefix upstream adds saves to a 400 the editor didn't warn about, or the editor refuses a name the server now accepts.

entries.why: Slash-command words a skill name may not be. Copied verbatim; the editor flags them on the Name field before Save.
entries.failure_mode: Same as skill-name-reserved-prefixes, for an exact word.

entries.why: How the reserved lists apply: against the lowercased name, prefixes by startsWith, words by exact match, after the kebab-case and 64-character checks.
entries.failure_mode: A changed matching rule (case, order, a new check) lets through names the server refuses, or flags names it accepts.

entries.why: The display title limit the editor enforces inline (and disables Save past).
entries.failure_mode: A raised limit blocks titles the server would take; a lowered one saves to a 400.

entries.why: The kebab-case shape a skill name must have; data-schemas' validateSkillName imports it from here. The editor flags a name that doesn't match on the Name field before Save.
entries.failure_mode: A widened pattern makes the editor refuse names the server takes; a narrowed one saves to a 400 the editor didn't warn about.

entries.why: The name length limit the editor enforces inline (and disables Save past).
entries.failure_mode: A raised limit blocks names the server would take; a lowered one saves to a 400.

entries.why: The description length limit the editor enforces inline (and disables Save past).
entries.failure_mode: A raised limit blocks descriptions the server would take; a lowered one saves to a 400.

entries.why: The SKILL.md body length limit the editor enforces inline (and disables Save past).
entries.failure_mode: A raised limit blocks bodies the server would take; a lowered one saves to a 400.

entries.why: Web shows the Skills panel only with role SKILLS.USE AND the agents `skills` capability. The drawer entry mirrors both halves.
entries.failure_mode: The drawer offers Skills on a server that injects none into any run, or hides it where web shows it.

entries.why: The image types `GET /api/skills/:id/files/*path?raw=true` serves inline; everything else it sends as an attachment. The file screen fetches the raw bytes and previews an image only for these types.
entries.failure_mode: A type upstream adds opens as "can't be shown as text" instead of a preview, or a type it drops is still fetched and decoded. Nothing errors.

entries.why: `GET /api/permissions/search-principals` refuses a trimmed query under 2 characters with a 400. The skill share sheet doesn't send one, and shows nothing for it rather than a search error.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream raises the minimum, a short query 400s and the share sheet shows "Search failed" with a Retry that can't succeed; if it lowers it, a 1-character search the server would answer is never sent.

entries.why: How many skill names one turn may carry in `manualSkills`. The server dedupes, then truncates past the cap with only a log line; the client caps the pending chips and the request at the same number.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream lowers the cap, picks past it are silently never primed while their chips and pills show; if it raises it, the client refuses picks the server would run.

entries.why: An ephemeral (non-agent) run gets skills only when `ephemeralAgent.skills` is on, unless a model spec set `skills_enabled`. A persisted agent ignores the flag and uses its own `skills_enabled`/scope. So a turn that names manual skills on a non-agent endpoint sends the flag itself, and an agents-endpoint turn sends none.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream scopes ephemeral runs differently, picked skills stop being primed (the turn runs without them) or the flag starts exposing the catalog where it should not. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Web strips `manualSkills` (and `ephemeralAgent`) on assistants endpoints. The client sends none there and leaves the pending chips staged.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream starts honouring skills on assistants, the client keeps withholding them; if it strips them on more endpoints, the client sends names that are dropped.

entries.why: A model spec with a `skills` key overrides the ephemeral agent's skills: `true` = full catalog, `false` = none, a list = only those names (an empty list resolves to none). The client hides the Skills toggle while such a spec is active and stops reading or writing the per-conversation value. The override is an inline `if` block inside `initializeClient`, not a declaration, so the whole file is watched. At v0.8.8 the client never sees the key: `GET /api/config` strips it (see `model-spec-skills-sanitized`), so this mapping is inert until upstream sends it.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream changes how a spec's `skills` applies, the toggle is hidden while it would matter (or shown while ignored), and the picker offers skills the run drops.

entries.why: `GET /api/config` (`api/server/routes/config.js`) passes the model specs through this sanitizer, which deletes every spec's `skills` key, so the client always decodes `skills` as absent. The spec-governed skills handling (`model-spec-skills`: hidden toggle, Off/Only picker filters) is kept as forward-compatible code and does nothing until this function stops deleting the key. The server still applies the spec's `skills` to the run, invisibly to the client.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream starts sending `skills`, the dormant spec handling switches on with no client change: the Skills toggle hides under such specs and picks outside the spec are refused. That is the intended behaviour, but it was never seen against a real server and must be checked when this region changes.

entries.why: Where web keeps the Skills toggle (`LAST_SKILLS_TOGGLE_<suffix>`): an existing conversation under its own id, a new chat under the shared `new` slot, or under `__defaults__` (`Constants.spec_defaults_key`) when model specs exist and none is selected; nothing while a spec is active, where `applyModelSpecEphemeralAgent` (client/src/utils/endpoints.ts) rebuilds the ephemeral agent with no `skills` key, so a spec chat starts off. The client keeps the same slots: while any spec is selected the value starts off and is never read, but a toggle in an existing conversation is still written to its own slot, as `useToolToggle` (client/src/hooks/Plugins/useToolToggle.ts) writes `LAST_SKILLS_TOGGLE_<id>` whatever the spec; while the active spec configures `skills` the row is hidden and nothing is read or written. The rule is spread through the provider's effects, so the whole file is watched.
entries.failure_mode: If web changes which slot a new chat or a spec-less chat reads, a fresh chat here starts with a different Skills setting than the same chat on web. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Where a Skills toggle is written: `useToolToggle`'s sync effect writes `LAST_SKILLS_TOGGLE_<conversationId>` (or `new`) on every change of a defined `ephemeralAgent.skills`, with no check for an active spec, and `handleChange` dual-writes the `storageContextKey` slot. The client writes an existing conversation's toggle to its own slot under a selected spec too (`SkillsToggleDelegate.set`), so clearing the spec reads the same value web does. The effect and the handler live in one hook, so the whole file is watched.
entries.failure_mode: If web stops writing the toggle while a spec is active (or writes it elsewhere), a conversation here comes back from a spec with a Skills setting web doesn't show. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Why a chat under a selected model spec starts with Skills off: web rebuilds the ephemeral agent from the spec on every spec change, and the rebuilt agent carries no `skills` key, nor does its per-conversation override map read `LAST_SKILLS_TOGGLE_`. The client mirrors that with `SkillsToggleSlot.SpecSelected` (starts off and reads nothing; a toggle in an existing conversation is still written to its slot, as web's write effect does).
entries.failure_mode: If web starts setting `skills` from the spec or restoring a stored skills value there, a spec chat here starts off where web starts on, and the run gets no skill catalog. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Which skills a persisted agent lets the composer picker offer: `skills_enabled` other than true offers none; an explicit `skills_scope` decides (`none` none, `all` the full catalog, else the agent's allowlist of ids); without one a non-empty allowlist limits and an empty one means the full catalog. Web's `$` popover reads the same resolver.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream changes the scope rules, the picker offers skills the agent's run drops (the pick is silently not primed) or hides skills the agent would run. Nothing errors.

entries.why: What web's `$` popover lists: active for the user, `userInvocable !== false`, inside a persisted agent's scope (failing closed while the agent is unknown), every page of the catalog. The composer's combined `/` + `$` picker offers skill rows by the same filter. The filter and the agent-scope memo both live in the component, so the whole file is watched.
entries.failure_mode: If web narrows or widens the popover, the picker here offers skills the server will not prime, or hides ones it would. Nothing errors.

entries.why: A skill invocation is a tool call named exactly `skill` with `args.skillName`; web routes it to `SkillCall` inside the tool-call dispatch of this file. Both chat dispatchers route the same name to SkillCallCard.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream renames the tool or the arg, skill calls fall back to the generic tool card (or read as "Ran skill"). Nothing errors.

entries.why: A manually picked skill's card is not streamed: after the run, `api/server/controllers/agents/client.js` unshifts the parts this builds (completed `skill` tool calls) onto the reply's content, so they reach the client only with the final message. The streaming reply therefore shows a "Running X" stand-in per pick until the FINAL event. The unshift call sits in a 5,000-line controller, so the builder it calls is what is watched.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream starts streaming these cards, each pick shows twice mid-stream (the stand-in and the live card); if it stops adding them, the stand-in vanishes at the end with no card in its place. Nothing errors.

entries.why: How many conversation starters the new-chat screen shows. `MAX_CONVO_STARTERS` is one member of the large `Constants` enum, so most changes to this block are unrelated; check only that member.
entries.failure_mode: The new-chat screen shows more or fewer starters than web does. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Which starters the new-chat screen offers: the agent's own, else the selected model spec's. Web computes it in this component, and the server never says which applies.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream changes the order, adds a source or drops one, mobile offers different starters than web for the same agent or spec, or none at all. Nothing errors.
